references.text: The preceding context describes who stands before the Lord to make the covenant—from the leaders to the foreigners in the camp.
Moses reminds the people that the covenant was made not only with their ancestors but also with those living today—a similar theme about the scope of the covenant across generations.
Continuation of the covenant speech, which includes future generations and their opportunity to turn back to the Lord.
Isaiah speaks of God's blessing upon descendants, showing the extension of the covenant to future generations.
Peter says that the promise applies to his listeners, their children, and all who are far off—an expansion of the covenant concept to coming generations and other peoples.
Jesus prays not only for the disciples but also for those who will come to believe through their message—future generations of believers.
God's covenant with Abraham includes his descendants in every generation, a fundamental example of the covenant's reach beyond those physically present.
